findings.title: Percent parsing discards signs and other valid numeric syntax
findings.body: The regex extracts the first unsigned decimal substring instead of converting the complete value before `%`. Confirmed results include `-25%` → `0.25`, `.5%` → `0.05`, and `1e2%` → `0.01`; junk such as `abc25%` is silently accepted, while `%` throws from `digits[0]`. This violates the required fraction conversion and can silently reverse or distort rates.
findings.recommendation: Remove only the trailing `%` and convert the entire remaining string, such as `Number(input.slice(0, -1)) / 100`, so Number-compatible signs and formats are preserved and junk is not partially accepted.

next_steps: Correct full-prefix percent conversion and verify signed, leading-decimal, exponent, and malformed inputs.
